The AIOps at NREL effort will be designed to work with the Delta system. Current data center cooling management systems do not take future IT load and behavior into account. Since there is a large amount of thermal inertia built into a large data center such as NREL’s, the system can take a long time to cool down or warm up. From the collected data streams (in year-1) on each application’s power profile, machine learning methods can be used to predict the footprint of each such job, whether they be capacity (single-node jobs) or capability (large-scale, multi-node jobs) or somewhere in between. Then apriori, we will have an idea on the impending power/energy footprints of the collection of jobs that will be scheduled to run, in which a maximum amount of the cooling resources will be needed to enable the job to successfully run, the ramp rate of the job will be much faster than the cooling system can get up to steady-state. This can lead to a sharp increase in power consumption as more and more cooling resources are added, which in turn can lead to a massive over-provisioning of cooling capacity. If the job suddenly consumes half of its peak power, the cooling infrastructure will continue to run at full capacity for a substantial amount of time since the cooling infrastructure cannot ramp down as rapidly as the IT system power can change. To prevent this, the cooling system can be ramped up ahead of time in anticipation of a large job coming online. Similarly, if the power profile is expected to drop, the cooling system will be ramped down at a prescribed rate in anticipation of the IT system ramping down. This ramping up/down of the cooling system can be done each day at the appropriate time, given the anticipated cooling needs of the job collection that’s expected to run or come online as scheduled. 3 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. The cooling system ramp time, amount, and type of cooling resources, etc. will be determined by the Data Analytics module. The adjustment to the cooling system will initially be done manually. At a later stage, the team will demonstrate autonomous control. Specifically, we will focus on the following tasks: • Establish power profiles from HPC applications • Investigate machine learning approaches to power aware scheduling. 3.2.2 Instrumentation resiliency, integrity, and anomaly detection NREL’s data center is highly instrumented. The instrumentation can sometimes drift, or malfunction, in ways that are difficult to detect. This task will focus on characterizing and tracking instrumentation behavior over time.
